Wells Fargo FTE Interview Experience 2022
Sushmey Nirmal
Final Year IT
Wells Fargo visited our college in August 2022. All circuit branches were allowed.
Initially, the CGPA criteria for the online test was >=6.75 but then they changed it to >=8.
4 rounds were conducted
1.
Online Assessment
2.
Technical Round
3.
Technical + Managerial Round
4.
HR Round
The whole process was conducted online.
Online Assessment
The Online Assessment was conducted on SHL (AMCAT) platform and had 3 sections as given
below. No negative marking. Free navigation wasn’t allowed in the first two sections.
Verbal Aptitude: Consists of 12 MCQs to be solved in 15 minutes. This section mostly tested
your English and ability to process information by asking questions based on given passages.
Important Tip: For comprehension, read the paragraph quickly, and be on the lookout for a
change in opinions, conclusions, or universally accepted facts mentioned in the passage. You
cannot use outside information, if it’s not mentioned in the passage then you can’t use it even if
it seems like the correct answer, look for a better answer which has been mentioned or hinted at
in the passage.
Business Acumen: Consists of 15 MCQs to be solved in 25 minutes.
In this section almost all questions were based on charts (i.e. candlestick chart, line chart, bar
chart, etc)You had to use the information in the chart and answer the questions.
Important Tip: Since free navigation is not allowed, just skip the questions you don’t get after a
little while. Time management is key. Trust your instincts!
Coding questions:
Two questions, 60 minutes, free navigation was allowed here so you can try questions out of
order. SHL AMCAT tests always need you to write the code to take input from the user yourself.
No amount of leetcoding will save you if you don’t know how to input data from the user.

Q1: You’re trying to code some video game queueing algorithm where the players pick random
numbers. You pick the largest and smallest number and pair them and then add the difference
as the score variable and then add back the value (of the difference, not the score variable) to
the array. You keep doing that until you have only one player remaining and finally return the
score variable.
If two players choose the same number, skip one of the same numbered players and go to the
next one.
The solution could be too big so return mod 100000007
Answer: The question is asking you to take the smallest and the largest and then add the
difference back to the array and repeat the same thing. You could sort the array and just get the
first and last elements but you’d need to sort the array every time. A better solution would be to
use minHeap and maxHeap. I managed to get 21/21 cases with this.
Q2: This question asked you to maximise the profits of cab drivers. You are given the number of
days and then the intercity and intracity travel rates for that day. You can pick intercity only if you
haven’t worked the previous day.
Answer: This can be solved using dynamic programming with memoization with a bottom-up
approach calculating the profit for each day as the final day. I managed to get 19/21 cases here.
Technical interview
22 people were selected for the interview round. The interviews were scheduled the next day
after the email with the shortlisted candidates was sent. Mine was at 9:50 AM.
A tip that always helps me with interviews is that interviewers are here to help us. Just try to
connect with them, make conversation about the weather or in some other benign way. Feel free
to ask for help if you feel stuck.
My interviewer started by asking me about myself, what tech stacks I’ve worked with etc.
Then he asked me about the difference between AngularJS and Angular since my resume
mentioned I’ve worked with Angular.
Then he asked me about SQL vs NoSQL DB because I had used SQL in a project of mine and
explained why I used NoSQL over SQL.
Note: Never mention stuff you wouldn’t be able to answer. Always frame your answers and try to
come up with questions that might be asked in relation to the answer you’re saying. For
example, if you say “Oh, I used x because x is better than y here” you’re practically forcing the
interviewer to ask about the “y” which you mentioned in the answer. This is good because it

makes interviews predictable, predictable means you can prepare for it in advance meaning
you’d come off more confident.
He also asked me about the types of keys
Then he asked me if I could answer Python questions (He turned out to be a Python developer)
because I had mentioned Python in my resume. I had honestly even forgotten that I had
mentioned Python in my resume. This could’ve been disastrous for me but I clarified that my
primary DSA Language is Java and I hadn’t worked with Python in a long time, but I’d be happy
to answer basic-level questions. He then asked me what the difference between lists and tuples
was.
Then he said “let’s move on to general questions, not language specific”
He asked me if I knew sorting algorithms and what sorting algorithm I’d use if I had a huge
array. I compared common sorting algorithms, provided sufficient reasons, and said I’d use
merge sort. He asked me why I’d use merge sort.
Then he asked me to explain the code of merge sort. As I was explaining merge sort I
mentioned how traditionally it is a recursive algorithm, which prompted him to ask if I knew what
recursion is, then he asked me the recursive code of a factorial. I explained it to him then he
asked me to continue explaining merge sort.
Then he asked me a puzzle. If I had 8 balls, all visually identical but one weighed more than the
rest, what’s the minimum number of comparisons I’d need with a beam balance to find the
heavier ball.
I didn’t know the solution nor had I ever seen a similar question like this before. That’s fine they
don’t expect you to know it. Approach the question how you’d approach it normally, speak your
steps out loud and if you realise your steps would fail, explain why they’d fail and try another
approach. I did this and reached a solution that I'd need a minimum of 3 comparisons. The
interviewer said the solution is 2 and asked me to try again. I still wasn’t able to come up with a
satisfactory solution but the interviewer said “you tried very well”
Then the interviewer asked if I had any questions for him. Always ask questions, it shows you’re
interested in the company.
I asked him how long he had been working in the company and then asked follow up questions
on the tech stack he said he had used, reverse interview lol. Then we got on to talking about the
Cloud and its application and he asked me if I knew what cloud computing is used for. This
provided another avenue to display what I knew and helped me make a better case for myself.
Technical + Managerial interview

This interview was about 10-15 minutes after the first one. This interview wasn’t very traditional
because he was trying to transfer data from one computer to another so asked me to wait
instead of asking me about myself. I used this opportunity to connect with the interviewer and
asked if he’d be okay with answering a few questions of mine. I asked him about his role in the
company and he happily answered.
He started by asking me about myself and then about my internship at Barclays.
Then asked me if I knew the four pillars of OOP with real-life examples.
He then asked me if I was given an array of subjects with teachers as attributes of each subject
where one teacher can teach multiple subjects, would I be able to sum up and return the number
of subjects taught by each teacher. He said I could take some time to understand and solve the
question. I then repeated the question back to him just to make sure I was understanding it
correctly. Then I explained how I’d do it verbally, which he then asked me to code. I coded on a
google doc and explained the dry run of the code. He seemed satisfied.
He then asked me what ‘I’ in ACID properties meant. Follow up questions were,
- what ‘C’ meant.
- if I knew what transactional locks mean?
Then he asked if I could write SQL queries, and asked me to write a query to find marks from
two tables inner join on a column.
Then asked me to display null values for the right column data.
Then asked me what my favourite subject was. Note: Make sure you’re able to answer
everything about whatever you’re mentioning here. Anything you mention in an interview is fair
game unless stated otherwise.
Then asked what three words define me, then asked me to explain why.
Finally, he asked me if I had any questions for him. Now even though I had already asked
questions in the beginning, I still asked a few questions.
HR Round (Telephonic)
This round was a long time after the previous one. 8 people were shortlisted for this round and
this round seemed mostly like a formality. The HR asked what my hobbies were and why I
wanted to work at Wells Fargo. I mentioned stuff I had read in their presentation and said I
wanted to work with new technologies. Then they asked if I had any questions for them.
They released the list of all selected FTEs immediately after this round and on the same day as
the interviews. I was delighted to see my name in the list!
